steps: Stand tall, eyes ahead, shoulders relaxed and arms bent about 90 degrees swinging forward and back.
Land with your foot close under your body and roll through quickly, with short, light steps.
Keep a steady breathing rhythm at a pace where you could still say a short sentence.
Running.mistake: Overstriding, reaching the foot far in front, which brakes every step and hammers the knees.

steps: Run tall with a slight forward lean from the ankles and relaxed hands.
Take short, quick steps landing under your hips, and let your arms swing gently.
Hold a pace that is easy enough to breathe through your nose or hold a conversation.
Jogging.mistake: Starting too fast and then fading, instead of settling into an easy pace you can hold.

steps: Walk tall with your chin level and shoulders back and relaxed.
Swing your bent arms from the shoulders and take quick, comfortable strides.
Land on your heel and roll through to push off with your toes, aiming for a pace that raises your breathing.
Brisk Walking.mistake: Strolling with short steps and still arms, which leaves your heart rate barely raised.

steps: Stand tall and drive your elbows back, with arms bent about 90 degrees.
Take quick, purposeful steps that roll heel to toe, pushing off strongly with the back foot.
Keep the pace high enough that you are breathing hard but can still talk in short phrases.
Power Walking.mistake: Overreaching with the front foot and leaning back, which slows the stride and strains the shins.

steps: Warm up with a few minutes of easy jogging and a couple of short build-ups first.
Sprint at close to full effort for the set time, driving your knees and arms hard.
Walk or jog easily to recover fully before the next sprint.
Sprint Intervals.mistake: Sprinting cold or cutting the recovery short, which makes each rep slower and raises injury risk.

steps: Pick a steady incline and warm up with easy jogging and a couple of short build-ups.
Lean slightly into the hill and drive hard with your knees and arms for the whole effort.
Walk back down slowly to recover fully before the next sprint.
Hill Sprints.mistake: Looking down at your feet and bending at the waist instead of leaning from the ankles.

steps: Start with a few minutes of easy running to warm up.
Mix in bursts of faster running of different lengths, picking landmarks like lamp posts as your start and finish.
Recover with easy jogging until you feel ready, then pick the next burst.
Fartlek Running.mistake: Making every burst all-out, so the later ones fall apart and the session becomes a slog.

steps: Hold the handles at hip height with your elbows close and turn the rope with your wrists.
Jump just high enough for the rope to pass, landing softly on the balls of your feet.
Keep a steady rhythm with your eyes forward and knees slightly bent.
Jump Rope.mistake: Jumping too high and turning the rope with the whole arms, which tires you out quickly.

steps: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart and your arms bent at your sides.
Run in place, driving each knee up to hip height while pumping your opposite arm.
Stay on the balls of your feet with your chest up and core tight.
High Knees.mistake: Leaning back and landing on the heels instead of staying tall on the balls of the feet.

steps: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart and your arms bent at your sides.
Jog in place, flicking each heel up toward your glutes.
Keep your knees pointing down and your hips level as you stay light on your feet.
Butt Kicks.mistake: Letting the knees swing forward so the move turns into a bouncy jog with no hamstring work.

steps: Start standing with your feet together and your arms by your sides.
Jump your feet out wide while swinging your arms overhead.
Jump back to the start and repeat at a steady rhythm, landing softly.
Jumping Jacks.mistake: Landing stiff-legged on the heels, which jars the knees and hips.

steps: Stand on one leg with a slight bend in the knee and your torso tilted forward.
Leap sideways to the other leg, swinging your arms across your body for balance.
Land softly on the new leg, absorb it with a bent knee and immediately leap back.
Skater Jumps.mistake: Landing on a straight leg or letting the knee cave in, which jolts the joint.

steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and swing your arms back as you sit your hips back.
Swing your arms forward and explode up and forward as far as you can.
Land softly with bent knees, hips back, and reset before the next jump.
Broad Jumps.mistake: Landing with straight legs or the chest collapsed, which sends the impact into the knees and back.

steps: Stand with your feet hip-width apart and your knees slightly bent.
Jump straight up and pull both knees toward your chest at the top.
Land softly on the balls of your feet with bent knees and reset before the next one.
Tuck Jumps.mistake: Rushing the next rep before the landing is stable, which causes sloppy, stiff landings.

steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart in a light stance, knees soft and hands up by your chin.
Throw jabs, crosses and hooks with your hips and shoulders turning into each punch.
Stay on the balls of your feet, moving around and breathing out with each punch.
Shadow Boxing.mistake: Throwing arm-only punches and locking the elbows hard at full extension.

steps: Do a burpee: squat, kick back to a plank, lower your chest, then jump your feet back in.
Explode into a jump with your arms overhead and land softly.
Move straight into the next exercise in the circuit and keep a steady pace.
Burpee Cardio Circuit.mistake: Letting the hips sag in the plank when tired, which puts the load on the lower back.

steps: Warm up first, then start at the bottom of a flight of stairs, leaning slightly forward.
Drive up two stairs at a time or one quickly, pumping your arms and pushing through the whole foot.
Walk back down carefully, one step at a time, and recover before the next climb.
Stair Sprints.mistake: Landing on your toes with your heels hanging off the step, which strains the calves and Achilles.

steps: Stand tall with your hands on your hips or arms swinging, feet hip-width apart.
Step forward into a lunge until both knees are about 90 degrees, then push off the front foot into the next step.
Keep moving at a steady pace with your chest up.
Walking Lunges Cardio.mistake: Taking short steps and letting the front knee drift far over the toes.

steps: Set two markers about 10 to 20 metres apart and warm up first.
Sprint to the far marker, plant one foot, touch the line and drive back.
Keep your steps short as you turn and rest between sets.
Sprint Shuttles.mistake: Turning on a straight, locked leg instead of bending the knee and pushing off the outside foot.

steps: Lay a ladder flat and stand at one end on the balls of your feet.
Step quickly in and out of each square in the pattern, keeping your steps short and light.
Look ahead, not down, and keep your arms pumping.
Agility Ladder Drills.mistake: Staring at your feet, which slows your rhythm and rounds your back.

steps: Stand on one leg with your knee slightly bent and your torso tilted forward.
Push off sideways to the other leg, covering as much distance as you can control.
Land softly on the new leg, hold for a beat and bound back.
Lateral Bounds.mistake: Rushing the landing, so the knee wobbles instead of absorbing the impact.

steps: Adjust the seat so your knee has a slight bend at the bottom of the pedal stroke.
Sit tall with a relaxed grip, and pedal in smooth circles at a steady cadence.
Add or reduce resistance to hold the effort you want.
Stationary Bike.mistake: A seat set too low, which puts stress on the knees and wastes power.

steps: Start at a slow speed, holding the rails only to step on, then let go.
Walk tall with your shoulders relaxed, arms swinging naturally and eyes ahead.
Increase the speed or incline until your breathing is a bit heavier, then hold it.
Treadmill Walk.mistake: Holding the handrails the whole time, which cuts the effort and throws off your posture.

steps: Warm up with a brisk walk, then raise the speed until you are jogging comfortably.
Run tall in the middle of the belt with your arms swinging and steps landing under your hips.
Set a pace you can hold, adding a 1 percent incline if you want it closer to road running.
Treadmill Jog.mistake: Running at the very front of the belt and reaching with the feet.

steps: Stand upright with your feet flat on the pedals and your hands lightly on the handles.
Push and pull in a smooth, controlled stride, keeping your weight over your hips.
Pick a resistance that keeps you working, and reverse direction now and then.
Home Elliptical.mistake: Leaning heavily on the handles, which removes most of the workload from your legs.

steps: Stand in front of a sturdy box with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Swing your arms back, sit your hips back, then jump up and land softly on the box with your whole foot.
Stand up tall and step down, rather than jumping down, then reset.
Box Jump.mistake: Choosing a box too high and landing in a deep squat, or jumping back down hard onto the knees.

steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, knees soft, and hold one rope end in each hand.
Make fast, alternating waves with your arms, driving from the shoulders and keeping your core tight.
Work in short bursts and breathe steadily.
Battle Ropes.mistake: Standing straight-legged and using only the wrists, which makes the waves small and strains the back.

steps: Stand facing a low step with your chest up and your abs braced.
Step up with one foot, bring the other up, and step down in a smooth, repeating pattern.
Land with your whole foot on the platform and keep your steps light.
Step Aerobics.mistake: Stepping so far back off the platform that you pull yourself off balance.

steps: Find a song or class with a steady beat and start with a gentle warm-up.
Move your whole body to the beat, keeping your knees soft and arms active.
Keep going without stopping, and scale the moves down if you are out of breath.
Dance Cardio.mistake: Standing stiffly and doing small movements, which keeps the effort too low.

steps: Stand in a light stance with your hands up and your knees slightly bent.
Combine punches and kicks, turning your hips and shoulders into each strike.
Stay light on your feet between strikes and keep your guard up.
Kickboxing Cardio.mistake: Kicking by locking the knee hard at full extension instead of snapping the leg back.

steps: Set the saddle so your knee has a slight bend at the bottom, and warm up spinning easily.
Add resistance and pedal hard for the work interval, staying smooth and keeping your upper body still.
Drop the resistance and spin easily to recover before the next interval.
Spin Bike Intervals.mistake: Gripping the handlebars tightly and bouncing on the saddle during the hard efforts.

steps: Pick 4 to 6 bodyweight moves like squats, jacks, high knees and mountain climbers.
Do each for a set time or reps with good form and move on with little rest.
Repeat the circuit for the rounds you planned, resting a minute between rounds.
Home Cardio Circuit.mistake: Rushing the first round so hard that form falls apart in the later ones.

steps: Set your saddle so your knee has a slight bend at the bottom of the stroke.
Keep your back relaxed, hands light on the bars, and pedal in smooth circles.
Change gears to hold a steady cadence and effort.
Cycling.mistake: Grinding in a hard gear at a low cadence, which strains the knees.

steps: Strap in, grab the handle with straight arms, and sit tall with your shins vertical.
Drive with your legs first, then lean back slightly and pull the handle to your lower ribs.
Reverse the order to return: arms out, torso forward, then bend the knees.
Rowing Machine.mistake: Pulling with the arms first and hunching, which loses most of the leg power.

steps: Stand upright with your hands lightly on the rails, feet fully on the steps.
Climb at a steady pace, pushing through your whole foot with each step.
Keep your chest up and let the rails guide balance, not carry your weight.
Stair Climber.mistake: Leaning on the rails and hunching forward, which cuts the work and strains the back.

steps: Stand tall with your feet flat on the pedals and your hands on the moving handles.
Push and pull smoothly through the stride, driving through your heels.
Choose a resistance that keeps you working, and switch direction now and then.
Elliptical Machine.mistake: Letting the knees collapse inward or hunching over the console.

steps: Warm up with easy running, then stand on the side rails while you set the sprint speed.
Step onto the belt and run hard for the interval, keeping your steps quick and landing under your hips.
Step back onto the side rails or slow to a walk to recover fully.
Treadmill Sprints.mistake: Stepping on at sprint speed from a standstill, which is easy to trip on.

steps: Push off the wall in a streamlined position, arms extended, face down.
Alternate your arms in smooth strokes, rotating your body, and kick from the hips.
Turn your head to breathe to the side every few strokes, keeping a steady rhythm.
Swimming Laps.mistake: Lifting the head to breathe, which sinks the hips and makes you work harder.

steps: Place your hands on the sled's uprights with straight arms and a flat back, leaning forward.
Drive hard with your legs in short, powerful steps, pushing the sled ahead.
Keep your hips low and your core braced the whole distance.
Sled Push.mistake: Standing too upright with the hips high, which wastes force into the ground.

steps: Adjust the seat so your knee has a slight bend, and sit tall.
Push and pull the handles with your arms while pedaling hard, in sync with your legs.
Pace the effort so you can keep going, with a steady rhythm of breathing.
Assault Bike.mistake: Sprinting out of the gate and fading, instead of building to a hard but even effort.

steps: Stand tall facing the machine, hands on the handles overhead.
Pull the handles down toward your thighs, hinging at the hips and bending your knees.
Return to standing as the handles rise, keeping the movement smooth.
Ski Erg.mistake: Pulling with the arms alone, which tires them fast, instead of using the hips and core.

steps: Step onto the pedals and take hold of the handles, standing tall.
Move opposite arm and leg together in a smooth climbing rhythm.
Keep your core tight, and use the full length of the reach.
Versaclimber.mistake: Taking short, choppy strokes, which lowers the workload and tires the shoulders.
